- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If supply net is strongly bearish (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates true drop; add 3–8% downward adjustment.
- When official events are frequent (≥18 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag in early days; shift forecast down by 1–3% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in 30d forecast.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and low sentiment, model often overpredicts early, then underpredicts later — use “event-weighted decay” to adjust forecast curve downward after day 10.
